title: Setting Up Your Docker Environment 💻
description: Install Docker Desktop and verify everything is working with docker version.

slides.title: Installing Docker Desktop 🛠️
slides.content:
# Choose Your Platform

- **Windows** / **macOS**: Download **Docker Desktop** from [docker.com](https://docker.com). It includes the daemon, client, Docker Compose and a friendly GUI.
- **Linux**: Install Docker Engine using your distribution’s package manager (e.g., `apt`, `yum`).

> Docker Desktop runs a lightweight Linux VM automatically, so containers work on any OS.

slides.title: Post‑Installation Checklist ✅
slides.content:
# After Installation

1. Open a terminal (Command Prompt, PowerShell, or your favourite shell).
2. Run:
   ```bash
   docker version
   ```
   You should see both **Client** and **Server** (daemon) version info.
3. Run:
   ```bash
   docker info
   ```
   This shows system‑wide information: number of containers, images, storage driver, etc.

If you see an error, make sure Docker Desktop is running.

quizData.question: True or False: `docker version` displays the version of the Docker client and the Docker daemon.
quizData.explanation: `docker version` shows separate information for the client (your CLI) and the server (the daemon). If the daemon isn’t running, the server section will be empty.

slides.title: No‑Root Setup 🔐
slides.content:
## Docker Group (Linux)

To avoid using `sudo` with every command, add your user to the `docker` group:
```bash
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
```
Then log out and back in.
